disclaimer: Entirely fictional. No real company, person, or agreement.

findings.title: Customer concentration materially understated
findings.expected_conclusion: Largest customer is 22.4% of FY2025 revenue; the CIM and the seller Q&A both state no customer exceeds 11%.
findings.anchor: seller_qa_log.csv row Q-011; Revenue_by_Customer_FY25.xlsx sheet FY25 row 3
findings.supporting_excerpt: No single customer exceeds 11% of revenue in FY2025.
acceptable_alternative_interpretations: Different period definition — rebutted: both sources state FY2025.

findings.title: Change-of-control consent required by largest customer
findings.expected_conclusion: The Lakeside master service agreement deems a >50% ownership change an assignment requiring prior written consent, which may be withheld at the customer's sole discretion, with a 30-day termination right. Not disclosed elsewhere in the room.
findings.supporting_excerpt: shall require the prior written consent of Customer, which consent may be withheld
acceptable_alternative_interpretations: Whether the clause is enforceable is a legal question and out of scope.

findings.title: Fixed charge coverage covenant not met
findings.expected_conclusion: FCCR computes to 1.18x against a 1.25x minimum in the credit agreement.
findings.supporting_excerpt: Fixed charge coverage ratio 1.18x / Required minimum under Section 6.11 1.25x
acceptable_alternative_interpretations: A waiver may exist but none is in the room — report as unresolved if asserted.

findings.title: Recurring revenue share unsupported as stated
findings.expected_conclusion: Management reports 78% recurring. Contracted maintenance revenue is 52.0% of FY2025 revenue. The KPI definitions note shows the 78% figure includes T&M work from contract-holding customers. Report as a definition difference, NOT as an error.
findings.anchor: KPI deck page 1 line 7; kpi_definitions.txt 'Recurring revenue'
findings.supporting_excerpt: Recurring revenue as a share of total 78%
acceptable_alternative_interpretations: Both figures are defensible under their stated definitions. The finding is the ambiguity, not a misstatement.

findings.title: Erie lease expired; premises held over month-to-month
findings.expected_conclusion: The Erie lease expired 2025-11-30 with no renewal option. Seller Q&A Q-019 and the management transcript both state all leases run through 2028 or later.
acceptable_alternative_interpretations: A renewal may have been executed and not supplied — then it is also a missing document.

findings.title: Aged receivables concentrated in one customer
findings.expected_conclusion: $612,400 of $3,402,000 receivables is over 90 days (18.0%), of which $341,200 is a single customer at 118 days. Seller Q&A states there are no collection issues.
findings.supporting_excerpt: There are no collection issues; aging is normal for the industry.
acceptable_alternative_interpretations: A reserve may exist in the balance sheet; AR is stated net.

findings.title: Field staff classified as contractors contrary to Q&A
findings.expected_conclusion: Roster shows 84 people; payroll summary shows 71 W-2 employees; a contractor schedule lists 13 1099 personnel performing field technician work. Seller Q&A states all field staff are employees.
findings.anchor: payroll_summary.txt line 3; contractor_schedule.csv rows 1–13; seller_qa_log.csv Q-022
findings.supporting_excerpt: All field staff are employees of the Company.
acceptable_alternative_interpretations: Worker classification is a legal and tax determination and is out of scope. Report the inconsistency only.

findings.title: Single-supplier dependency with 60-day termination
findings.expected_conclusion: Hartwell Supply is 61.3% of parts cost of revenue and may terminate for convenience on 60 days notice.
findings.anchor: top_vendor_schedule.txt lines 3–4; Hartwell agreement page 1 Section 11.2
findings.supporting_excerpt: Either party may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon sixty (60) days
acceptable_alternative_interpretations: Alternate distributors may exist; not evidenced in the room.

findings.title: Unbilled work in process grew far faster than revenue
findings.expected_conclusion: WIP rose from $410,000 to $1,020,000 (148.8%) while revenue grew 8.5%.
findings.anchor: wip_schedule.txt lines 3–5; balance sheet page 2 notes
acceptable_alternative_interpretations: A large project in progress at year end could explain it; no such project is evidenced.

findings.title: Umbrella policy expiring with no renewal evidence
findings.expected_conclusion: Umbrella policy UM-40311 expires 2026-01-15. The renewal confirmation covers GL and auto and explicitly excludes the umbrella. No renewal certificate is in the room.
findings.supporting_excerpt: The umbrella policy UM-40311 is NOT included in this renewal confirmation.
acceptable_alternative_interpretations: It may have been renewed and simply not supplied.

findings.title: Litigation summary contradicted by counsel invoice
findings.expected_conclusion: The litigation summary states no pending matters. A November 2025 legal invoice bills time on a 'Mercer arbitration', and the management transcript refers to it.
findings.supporting_excerpt: Review of Mercer arbitration demand and response strategy
acceptable_alternative_interpretations: The matter may have concluded between the invoice and the summary date.

findings.title: Capex and fixed asset registers disagree
findings.expected_conclusion: Capex register lists 5 FY2025 vehicle additions totalling $487,000; the fixed asset register shows 3 additions totalling $312,000. One asset is also recorded at two different costs.
acceptable_alternative_interpretations: Timing: assets ordered in FY2025 may be placed in service in FY2026.

findings.title: Two revenue schedules with different totals
findings.expected_conclusion: Two FY25 revenue-by-customer workbooks differ by $118,000 on one customer with no revision marks or dates. R2 later withdraws the v2 file.
acceptable_alternative_interpretations: After R2 the original is the schedule of record; before R2 it is genuinely ambiguous.

findings.title: FY2024 financial statements not supplied
findings.expected_conclusion: Request item 2.2 asks for FY2024 statements. They are absent, and the seller Q&A response is 'Will follow'. R2 states they are not available in final form.
findings.supporting_excerpt: Not available in final form; management accounts only.
acceptable_alternative_interpretations: Management accounts may be acceptable; that is a buyer decision.

findings.title: Referenced Exhibit B absent from baseline room
findings.expected_conclusion: The Hartwell agreement incorporates Exhibit B pricing by reference. Exhibit B is not in R1. Disposition must be NOT FOUND (referenced but absent), not MISSING (requested but not supplied) — it was never on the request list.
findings.supporting_excerpt: Distributor pricing is set out in Exhibit B, attached hereto and incorporated
acceptable_alternative_interpretations: In R2 an Exhibit B appears but names a different entity — see RDG-022.

findings.title: Branch gross margin overstated in KPI reporting
findings.expected_conclusion: Fort Wayne gross margin computes to 28.7% from the trial balance; the KPI deck reports 34.2%.
findings.anchor: KPI deck page 1 line 4; trial_balance.csv rows for branch FTW accounts 4000 and 5000
acceptable_alternative_interpretations: Branch reporting may allocate overhead differently; no allocation policy is supplied.

findings.title: Equipment revenue recognized on order, not shipment
findings.expected_conclusion: The stated policy records equipment sales when a purchase order is accepted. Three December 2025 orders totalling $284,000 shipped in January 2026.
findings.supporting_excerpt: equipment sales are recorded when a customer purchase order is accepted
acceptable_alternative_interpretations: Whether this is GAAP-compliant is an accounting judgment and is out of scope; refer to the QoE provider.

findings.title: Entity name inconsistent across records
findings.expected_conclusion: The articles read 'Ridgeline Industrial Services, LLC'. The ownership schedule reads 'Ridgeline Industrial Service LLC'. Do not infer a separate entity.
findings.anchor: Articles page 1 line 2; ownership_schedule.csv column entity_name_as_written
acceptable_alternative_interpretations: Clerical variation is the likeliest explanation.

findings.title: Customer identifier zero-padding lost
findings.expected_conclusion: customer_master.csv preserves '000418'; the revenue workbook stores 418. Joining on the raw value will not match.
findings.anchor: customer_master.csv row 1 column customer_id; workbook sheet FY25 row 3 column A

findings.title: Employee roster data quality defects
findings.expected_conclusion: Four roster rows have blank hire dates and two employee IDs are duplicated.
findings.anchor: sheet Roster rows 14, 35, 53, 72 (blank hire_date); rows 9/42 and 21/64 (duplicate ids)

findings.title: Tax support archive cannot be opened
findings.expected_conclusion: The encrypted archive is UNREVIEWED, not MISSING. It was supplied; it cannot be processed. Reporting it as missing would send the buyer to request a document the seller already provided.
acceptable_alternative_interpretations: None. This disposition is binary and is a scored trap.

findings.title: R2 Exhibit B names a different contracting entity
findings.expected_conclusion: The Exhibit B added in R2 names 'RIDGELINE INDUSTRIAL SERVICES OF OHIO, LLC', which is neither the contracting party in the agreement nor the entity in the articles. RDG-015 must not be marked resolved.
findings.supporting_excerpt: RIDGELINE INDUSTRIAL SERVICES OF OHIO, LLC
acceptable_alternative_interpretations: Could be a drafting error; either way the original request is not satisfied.

negative_controls.title: Active vs all customer counts differ (142 vs 143)
negative_controls.why_tempting: Looks like a reconciliation break between the KPI deck and the customer master.
negative_controls.correct_behavior: No finding. kpi_definitions.txt defines both terms and states 143 records / 142 active.

negative_controls.title: Churned customer shows zero FY25 revenue
negative_controls.why_tempting: A zero looks like missing data.
negative_controls.correct_behavior: No finding. The churn log documents the 2025-04 plant closure.

negative_controls.title: Two identical-looking fuel journal entries
negative_controls.why_tempting: Same amount, same date, same branch — looks like a duplicate posting.
negative_controls.correct_behavior: No finding. Journal ids JE-ERI-6205 and JE-ERI-6206 are distinct accounts.

negative_controls.title: Two identical payroll journal rows in Toledo
negative_controls.correct_behavior: This IS reportable as a data-quality observation (Low). It is included to test that the operator distinguishes it from NC-003, which is not.

negative_controls.title: Request item 10.3 marked 'Not applicable'
negative_controls.why_tempting: An N/A on a request list usually needs chasing.
negative_controls.correct_behavior: No finding. Written rationale and a buyer confirmation date are supplied.

negative_controls.title: GL and auto certificates expire 2026-01-15
negative_controls.why_tempting: Two expiring policies look like an insurance gap.
negative_controls.correct_behavior: No finding. The renewal notice confirms both. Only the umbrella is unrenewed (RDG-010).

negative_controls.title: Northgate agreement references Exhibit A
negative_controls.why_tempting: A referenced exhibit is often absent — the pattern of RDG-015.
negative_controls.correct_behavior: No finding. Northgate_Exhibit_A_Pricing.txt is present in the room.

negative_controls.title: Erie branch has no branch manager on the roster
negative_controls.why_tempting: Looks like a key-person gap or a roster omission.
negative_controls.correct_behavior: No finding. The org chart footnotes the shared role with Fort Wayne since 2024.

negative_controls.title: CIM-style rounding of revenue to $16.4M
negative_controls.correct_behavior: No finding. Rounding within an obvious tolerance is not a discrepancy.

negative_controls.title: Date formats differ between capex and fixed asset registers
negative_controls.why_tempting: Format variation often signals a parse problem.
negative_controls.correct_behavior: No finding. All dates parse unambiguously to the same calendar dates.

negative_controls.title: Toledo lease expires 2029, outside the diligence window
negative_controls.why_tempting: An expiry date invites a lease-term finding.
negative_controls.correct_behavior: No finding. Ten-year term with a renewal option; nothing inconsistent.

negative_controls.title: Legal invoice contains a 0.062-hour line
negative_controls.why_tempting: An odd fractional entry looks like a data error.
negative_controls.correct_behavior: No finding. Immaterial and internally consistent.
